message.content:
To terminate Visual Studio Code from the command line you can use the Windows `taskkill` utility.  
If VS Code’s executable is named **code.exe** (the default), run:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

Explanation of the switches:

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Specifies the image name (process name) – here `code.exe`. |
| `/F`   | Forces termination (equivalent to “kill”). |

**Notes**

* If you’re running this from a normal user account and VS Code was launched with elevated privileges, you may need to run the command prompt as Administrator (`Run as administrator`) to see and kill the process.
* You can also list all running processes first to confirm the exact image name:

  ```cmd
  tasklist | findstr /i code
  ```

  This will show entries like `code.exe` along with their PID.

That single command will immediately stop all instances of VS Code that match the image name.
